newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong couples rush to marry before flag change.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong couples rush to marry before flag change.

text.p: Hundreds of lovers have been rushing to Hong Kong's marriage registries, queueing for days and nights on end, to book a wedding date on the eve of the end of British colonial rule.
The eager couples were anxious to clinch what will be the last marriage certificates emblazoned with the British crown.

"I am very happy now. I've been waiting for days and it's paid off," Li Chin-hung told reporters after he had signed up to marry his sweetheart on June 29, the last working day for the registries before Britain turns Hong Kong over to China.
He was one of many young people who queued up in camping clothes, armed with books and portable radios with headphones to kill time.
Not only is it the last wedding day under British rule, but June 29 is also an auspicious day for weddings, according to Chinese astrologers.
Some couples even hired students to line up for them. "Many people were queuing up," said an official at the registration authority.
Marriage registries will be closed on June 30, a public holiday to mark the sovereignty transfer. China takes over in the first second of July 1.
Restaurants, including those in hotels, are almost fully booked on June 29 for wedding banquets, catering industry sources say.
